articles.title: From Hookups to CRMs: How the Web Summit Generation Grew Up
articles.summary: In the Old West a rumor would run about a spot with gold, somewhere in the wilderness. Hundreds, sometimes thousands of people would hit the road and join the place. The prospectors would go and dig the dirt, and buy their dinner with the gold they found during the day. Or have no dinner if they didn't find any. Most of these cities disappeared once the gold ran out. Some of them became permanent settlements and entered the legend. My first Web Summit was in 2024. It was wild. My founder booked us tickets, took an Airbnb, put a bundle of banknotes in an empty candy box for the local expenses, and we found ourselves with tens of thousands of similar men and women in a big conference room with badges, all chasing hype, money and adventure. Web Summit looks on the surface like a normal tech conference. Yet it's the first one that institutionalized the “Night Summit”, an informal workation play zone with musicians and foosball tables rocking the scene from 6 to 10pm. After the “Night Summit” you had the parties that would go until the morning. It's also a place that helped propel startups like Stripe, Uber, Revolut, Datadog, Twilio and ElevenLabs, helping them expand their market share

articles.title: World of Warcraft: Forever isn't mere nostalgia bait - it's rebuilding the MMO social architecture that Blizzard spent years dismantling
articles.summary: I don't play video games regularly anymore. Not because I've lost interest in them, but because I no longer make the time, the premium on which has seemed to exponentiate with age. I realised, however, in 2019 that I was a kind of sleeper agent: whenever I heard the opening notes of Legends of Azeroth , the original World of Warcraft login screen music, I would feel the reactivation of a latent part of my mind laid down when I was 10 years old. And so, like a form of possession, whenever Blizzard announces a new legacy iteration of the original WoW, no downpayment in time nor money is too great to prevent me from returning. Here I am, then, at the launch of World of Warcraft: Forever, seven years after Blizzard first revived the original 2004 game with World of Warcraft Classic in 2019. Once more I set foot on Durotar, to spend as much time as I can levelling up a new Orc Warrior before I am forcibly unplugged by either my boss or, more likely, my wife, and so far it's been a welcome return to some of the frictional - but more involving and consequential - socialising that WoW's decades of updates had previously sanded down. Java широко распространена в Южной Корее: по данным исследования JetBrains, на этот язык приходится 53% его использования в стране против среднемировых 30%. В государственных информационных системах показатель достигает 72%. Java применяется в банковской сфере Южной Кореи, корпоративных сервисах и государственных структурах, поэтому последствия успешной атаки могут затронуть критически важную инфраструктуру.
